parties.respondent: The Secretary To The Government of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare & Ors.

summary: The appellant challenged the validity of certain provisions of the National Medical Commission (Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate) Regulations, 2021 and the NMC (Compulsory Rotating Medical Internship) Regulations, 2021, on grounds of violation of Articles 14, 19(1)(g), and 21 of the Constitution. The provisions required foreign medical graduates to meet specific educational and internship criteria, including a 54-month course, 12-month foreign internship, registration in the host country, and a 12-month supervised internship in India. The appellant argued these imposed arbitrary, extra-territorial, and discriminatory requirements, restricted the right to practice medicine, and created unequal treatment between Indian and foreign medical graduates. The Court rejected the challenges, holding the regulations were within statutory authority, aimed at maintaining medical education standards, and were justified by past abuse and public interest. The Court upheld the regulations as reasonable and not ultra vires.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 15(4) read with Section 57 of the National Medical Commission Act
